title: Diagnose and recover targeted PostgreSQL lock contention
trigger: A customer write is blocked while PostgreSQL remains reachable and session evidence indicates a lock wait.
preconditions: confirm customer/business impact and the blocked operation
confirm the database is reachable and the issue is not connection exhaustion or a database-wide outage
identify the waiting backend and confirm wait_event_type=Lock
use pg_blocking_pids() and pg_locks to prove the exact blocker relationship
identify transaction/application context for the blocker before any termination
obtain required simulated approval for targeted backend termination
diagnostic_steps: inspect pg_stat_activity for waiting and active transactions
capture waiter pid, application_name, state, wait_event_type and wait_event
inspect pg_locks for holder/waiter lock modes and granted state
check transaction age and recent changes
do not classify a session as the blocker merely because it is old
mitigation_steps: if approval exists and evidence identifies one safe application blocker, terminate only that backend
do not restart PostgreSQL to clear a row-level lock
do not terminate unknown system, replication, migration, backup, or maintenance sessions without escalation
validation_steps: previously blocked customer transaction completes successfully
wait_event_type=Lock is no longer present for the exercise sessions
pg_blocking_pids() no longer reports the blocker chain
an independent follow-up write completes within the expected lock timeout
no unrelated database health regression appears after recovery
escalation_boundary: Escalate to DBA/development/change authority for unknown blocker ownership, schema migration or maintenance sessions, replication-sensitive work, multi-level blocking chains, repeated contention, deadlocks, inability to terminate safely, or contention that returns after the approved targeted action. OPSFORGE's pg_terminate_backend step represents a controlled simulated recovery and is not a claim of unrestricted L2 production privileges.
